candidates: When a component conditionally renders a native `<button>` element — for example, via a polymorphic `as` prop switching from `'a'` to `'button'` when no `href` is provided — always set `type="button"` explicitly. Without it, the HTML default is `type="submit"`, which silently triggers form submissions when the element is placed inside a `<form>`. Other button-based components in this codebase consistently use explicit `type="button"`; new code should follow the same convention.

When checking whether an optional string prop is absent, use an explicit `!= null` (or `=== undefined`) comparison rather than a JavaScript truthiness check. A truthiness check incorrectly treats a falsy-but-valid value such as an empty string (`href=""`) as absent, silently changing rendered output for callers who pass such values.

When writing or reviewing prose in documentation files (e.g., `MIGRATION.md`) and JSDoc comments, verify correct English article usage: use "an" before words that begin with a vowel sound (e.g., "an HTML element", "an API call"), not "a".
